theater: 蘇美爾南部（拉加什—烏瑪）

battle.name: 第一次烏瑪獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 蘇美爾南部（拉加什—烏瑪）
battle.brief: 前2450年前後，蘇美爾城邦烏瑪在執政者烏爾盧瑪率領下反抗拉加什的霸權，爭端源於兩城之間穆杜格灌溉渠的引水權。拉加什的執政者恩安那圖姆集結步兵與新近傳入的戰車，數戰之後擊敗烏瑪，逼其接受神廟仲裁與和約。列陣者手中所持，正屬卡面所示的銅矛頭長矛一類。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場衝突發生在公元前2450年前後的南部美索不達米亞，交戰的兩方是兩個各自獨立的蘇美爾城邦：位於西側、靠近幼發拉下游的拉加什，以及位於東側、接近底格里斯河道的烏瑪。拉加什此時由該城第一王朝的恩西（蘇美爾語 ensi，即城邦執政者，實權近似世襲君主）統治，在位者是恩安那圖姆；他的兄弟埃安那圖姆曾以《禿鷹碑》所記的戰役打敗烏瑪、烏爾與基什的聯軍，令拉加什在南部平原取得壓倒性的城邦優勢。烏瑪一方則由執政者烏爾盧瑪率領，烏瑪雖有城牆、神廟與自己的守護神，在實力上仍被視為拉加什的附庸。兩城的行政與軍事編制極簡：沒有常備軍，戰時由城內居民按戶、按工坊徵召，城官負責配水、啟閉城門與分配土地；神廟同時是倉房、工坊與帳房，神職人員執行文書、測量與審判；統治的合法性寫在泥板與石刻上，歷代執政者都以在神前立誓、修復廟宇、劃定水界作為施政的憑據。當時南部美索不達米亞仍是多城並立的格局，烏魯克、基什、烏爾、拉薩、尼普爾、阿克沙克等城各有附庸，而將要一統兩河的阿卡德尚未興起；烏瑪所謂的獨立，正是在這個諸城互相忌憚又互相結盟的格局裡提出來的。
countriesEn: This conflict broke out in southern Mesopotamia around 2450 BC, and the two sides were two independent Sumerian city-states: Lagash on the western side of the alluvial plain, near the lower Euphrates, and Umma on the eastern side, close to the channels of the Tigris. Lagash was then governed by the first dynasty of Lagash under an ensi - the Sumerian title for a city ruler whose office was in practice hereditary - and the ruler was Enannatum. His brother Eannatum had defeated a coalition of Umma, Ur and Kish in the campaigns recorded on the Stele of Vultures, and that victory had left Lagash with an overwhelming advantage over the southern plain. Umma was led by its own ensi, Ur-Lumma. Although Umma possessed walls, temples and a patron deity of its own, it was still treated in practice as a dependent of Lagash. The administration and the military organisation of both cities were extremely simple. There were no standing armies: in time of war the citizens were mustered household by household and workshop by workshop, while the city officers distributed water, opened and closed the gates and allotted land. The temples were at once granaries, workshops and account houses, and the priesthood carried out the writing, the surveying and the judging. Claims to rule were inscribed on clay tablets and on stone, and every ruler legitimised his authority by swearing before the gods, rebuilding the sanctuaries and marking out the water boundaries. Southern Mesopotamia was at that time a landscape of many rival cities: Uruk, Kish, Ur, Larsa, Nippur, Akshak and others each had their own alignments, while Akkad, the city that was to unite the two rivers, had not yet risen. Umma's 'independence' was therefore a claim made inside this world of mutually suspicious and mutually allied cities.
people: 拉加什方面的核心人物是恩安那圖姆（Enannatum I，約前2425年在位），他是阿庫爾伽爾之子、埃安那圖姆之弟，兄弟先後執掌拉加什的恩西之位。大英博物館收藏的泥板與來自吉爾蘇的石板上記有他的名號：石板以楔形文字寫著拉加什的恩西恩安那圖姆，正面刻出他執矛的側身像，年代約前2420年；另一件為寧基爾蘇造殿的銅鎚首上，刻著工匠巴拉基蘇蒙把器物奉獻給主人的祝辭，銘文提到恩安那圖姆曾為寧基爾蘇建造殿堂；大英博物館另藏一柄銅斧，上刻寧基爾蘇之名，是拉加什祭祀與戰爭兩用的器物。烏瑪方面是烏爾盧瑪（Ur-Lumma），他以執政者的身分挑起這場獨立戰爭；兵敗之後，烏瑪改由祭司出身的君主伊爾（Il）接掌，此人隨即再攻拉加什，開啟第二次獨立戰爭，最後在拉加什的恩特梅納（Entemena，即恩安那圖姆之子）手下被平定。上一代的身影也縈繞在戰局裡：埃安那圖姆（Eannatum）以《禿鷹碑》記載自己封堵穆杜格渠、把挖渠者投入水中的戰績，那份權威正是烏瑪這次挑戰的對象。事件的另一位當事人是神：拉加什的守護神寧基爾蘇被寫進和約文本，作為仲裁者與雙方的見證。現代層面上，1930年代考古者弗朗索瓦·馬里耶·阿洛特·德·拉·菲耶在烏瑪城西南的美沙（Mesha）發現記載和約的楔形文字泥板，這塊泥板成為今日重建這場戰爭的主要依據。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Lagash side was Enannatum (Enannatum I, in power around 2425 BC), son of Akurgal and younger brother of Eannatum, who had succeeded one another in the office of ensi of Lagash. His name is preserved on a clay tablet and on a stone plaque from Girsu in the British Museum: the plaque is inscribed in cuneiform with the words 'Enannatum, ensi of Lagash' and shows his profile holding a spear, and is dated to around 2420 BC. On a copper mace head dedicated for the construction of a temple of Ningirsu, the craftsman Barakisumun inscribed a dedicatory formula in which Enannatum is credited with having built a shrine for Ningirsu; the British Museum also holds a copper axe inscribed with the name of Ningirsu, an object used both in the cult of Lagash and in its fighting. On the Umma side stands Ur-Lumma, who as ensi launched this war of independence. After his defeat Umma was taken over by Il, a ruler of priestly origin, who at once attacked Lagash again and so opened the second war of independence; that war was finally crushed by Lagash under Entemena, the son of Enannatum. The previous generation still hovered over the field: Eannatum recorded on the Stele of Vultures how he dammed the Mu-dug canal and threw the excavators into the water, and that prestige was precisely what Umma now challenged. The other party to the affair was a god: Ningirsu, the patron deity of Lagash, was written into the treaty text as the adjudicator and as the witness of both sides. On the modern side, the archaeologist François Marie Allotte de la Fuÿe recovered in the 1930s a cuneiform tablet recording the peace terms at Mesha, to the south-west of Umma, and that tablet remains the principal basis for reconstructing the war today.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。它屬於青銅時代早段的通用形制，尾端常另加石或銅製的尾鐓，以免刺穿地面，矛頭與杆的接合處另以纏束加固。這種形制在同時期的蘇美爾與埃及其他地區同樣常見，兩河流域的長矛既可擲出，也可抵近格鬥，與卡面武器同出一脈。需要說明的是，這件埃及長矛本身並無出土於拉加什或烏瑪的證據，戰場上真正出現的是蘇美爾本地製作的同型長矛：考古所見這類銅矛頭形如柳葉，裝在約兩至三公尺的杆上，與皮或柳條包紗的長方形盾牌相配。除長矛之外，兩軍步兵還使用銅斧、鎚形斧、石片與黑曜石製的刀片、投石索與石彈；弓箭亦已出現，銅製或石製箭鏃是常見的消耗品。鎚形斧頭在這段時期同時是禮器與兵器，現存一件拉加什出土、上刻寧基爾蘇之名的銅斧即是此例。防護方面除盾牌外，貴族與軍官佩戴銅盔，《禿鷹碑》上引導步兵的埃安那圖姆便戴著一頂包銅的頭盔。投射與交通方面，當時的戰車剛剛傳入南部美索不達米亞，由驢或野驢拉挽而非真馬，戰車與矛兵方陣配合使用；糧秣、築城工具與建材靠驢車與河道船隻自幼發拉與底格里斯調運。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian spear: a spear of the early dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls and later to recover lost ground. It belongs to the general form of the early Bronze Age, with a stone or copper butt-spike at the lower end so that the shaft does not dig into the ground, and the head bound to the shaft with lashings. The same form is found in Sumer and in Egypt of the same period: the spears of the river valleys could be thrown and could also be used at close quarters, and they are of one line with the weapon on the card. It must be said that there is no evidence for the Egyptian spear itself at Lagash or at Umma; what actually stood on the field were spears of the same type made in Sumer itself, with copper heads shaped like willow leaves and set on shafts of roughly two to three metres, and used together with rectangular shields of hide or wicker. Beyond spears, the infantry of both armies carried copper axes, axe-heads, blades of flint and obsidian, slings and stone shot. Bows and arrows were also in use, with copper or stone arrowheads as the common expendable item. The axe-head was at that time both a ritual object and a weapon, and a copper axe from Lagash inscribed with the name of Ningirsu is a surviving example. For protection, besides the shield, nobles and officers wore copper helmets; on the Stele of Vultures the Eannatum who leads the infantry wears a copper-plated helmet. For mobility and transport, the war chariot had only just reached southern Mesopotamia and was drawn by donkeys or onagers rather than by horses, the chariots operating in combination with the phalanx of spearmen; grain, siege tools and building material were moved by donkey carts and by river boats on the Euphrates and the Tigris.
tactics: 拉加什的戰法建立在三件事上：城邦的集結、灌溉地的水戰、與神廟的名分。徵召來的步兵排成密集的橫隊，矛尖朝前，靠整齊的推進與身後的盾牆互相保護；一旦短兵相接，陣形轉為纏鬥，仍以矛、斧、鎚近身擊刺。開戰之前，拉加什先把烏瑪引往爭議地帶的穆杜格渠堵住，必要時直接斷水——在灌溉經濟裡，截斷對方水源與攻破城牆同樣致命，這也是埃安那圖姆在《禿鷹碑》上特別記錄的動作。戰車被用來做高速衝鋒與追擊，由驢拉的輕車在平坦沖積平原上速度有限，但足以威嚇與驅散對手，車兵與步兵之間靠號角與旗幟保持聯繫。烏瑪的守方依托城牆、渠堤與神廟高地，以弓矢與投石消耗進攻方，伺機反擊。戰事結束後，勝方並未吞併對方城池，而是走一套神判程序：把爭端提交拉加什的守護神寧基爾蘇，宣稱裁決出自神口；再用界碑標定疆界、重新規劃渠道，並以金銀賠償雙方都能接受的損失。這套把軍事勝利轉化為神聖條約的做法，正是這場戰爭在戰術史之外最值得留意的地方。
tacticsEn: The way Lagash fought rested on three things: the mustering of the city, water warfare in an irrigated landscape, and the authority of the temple. The infantry were drawn up in dense ranks with the spear points forward, protected by the ordered advance and by the wall of shields behind them; once the fighting closed, the line dissolved into a mêlée in which spear, axe and axe-head did the work at arm's length. Before the fighting opened, Lagash dammed the Mu-dug canal in the disputed ground and, if necessary, cut the water off outright; in an irrigated economy, depriving an enemy of water was as decisive as breaching a wall, and it is precisely this act that Eannatum singled out for record on the Stele of Vultures. Chariots were used for the fast charge and for pursuit; a light vehicle drawn by donkeys had limited speed on the flat alluvium but was enough to overawe and to scatter a formation, and the chariot crews kept contact with the foot through horns and banners. Umma's defenders, supported by the city wall, the canal banks and the raised ground of the temple precinct, wore down the attackers with arrows and slung stones and waited for their chance to counter-attack. When the fighting was over the victors did not annex the opposing city. They went through a process of divine judgement: the dispute was laid before Ningirsu, the patron god of Lagash, and the decision was declared to come from the god's mouth. Boundaries were then fixed with boundary stelae, the canals were replanned, and the losses were compensated in silver and gold in a form both sides could accept. This procedure of converting a military victory into a sacred treaty is the part of this war that deserves attention beyond the tactics themselves.
data: 關於數字，可以確定的與必須保留的空白都很清楚。年代方面，這場第一次烏瑪獨立戰爭一般定於公元前2450年前後，恩安那圖姆的在位年代約為前2425年；同一份戰爭年表也把烏瑪第一次獨立戰爭標在約前2400年，差異來自學界對《禿鷹碑》與恩安那圖姆泥板斷代的處理不一。地理上，拉加什（今日 Tell al-Hiba，阿爾希巴）與烏瑪（今日 Tell Jokha，捷喬哈）相距約十五至二十公里，戰線即兩城之間的灌溉渠地帶；用阿卡德語書寫的和約泥板於1930年代出土於烏瑪城西南的美沙。補償的數目是可查的：白銀一邁納與黃金一邁納，一邁納約六十舍客勒，折合半公斤上下，數目不大，反映雙方實力接近，勝負並非壓倒性的樣子。戰役次數只留下數戰這類模糊說法，雙方的兵力、陣亡與俘虜數目在蘇美爾的編年與銘文中都沒有留下可靠記載；同期城邦戰爭的規模往往只能從城牆範圍、墓葬分布與銘文提及的戰利品線索去推想，這一場也不例外。武器方面有一項可核對的旁證：《禿鷹碑》殘件今分藏於羅浮宮與伊拉克博物館，碑上以禿鷹銜著人類首級的意象記載戰果，說明雙方都按當時習俗把首級作為勝利與獻祭的憑證。
dataEn: As for numbers, both what can be established and what must be left blank are clear. On the date, this first war of independence of Umma is generally placed around 2450 BC, and the reign of Enannatum is dated to about 2425 BC; the same list of wars marks the first war of independence of Umma at about 2400 BC, and the discrepancy comes from differing scholarly treatment of the date of the Stele of Vultures and of the Enannatum tablets. On the ground, Lagash (modern Tell al-Hiba, al-Hiba) and Umma (modern Tell Jokha) lie about fifteen to twenty kilometres apart, and the front ran through the belt of irrigation canals between the two cities; the peace tablet, written in Akkadian, was excavated in the 1930s at Mesha to the south-west of the city of Umma. The amount of compensation can be checked: one mina of silver and one mina of gold, a mina being about sixty shekels or roughly half a kilogram, a modest figure that shows how close the two cities were in strength and how far from decisive the outcome was. The number of engagements survives only as a vague 'several battles'; no reliable figures for the size of the armies, for the dead or for the prisoners are preserved in the Sumerian chronicles or inscriptions. The scale of contemporary city-state wars can generally only be inferred from the extent of the walls, from the distribution of the cemeteries and from hints about booty in the inscriptions, and this war is no exception. On the materiel there is one verifiable side-evidence: the fragments of the Stele of Vultures are now divided between the Louvre and the Iraq Museum, and on the stele the victory is reported in the image of vultures carrying human heads, which shows that both sides followed the custom of treating the head as the proof of victory and of sacrifice.
cause: 起因要從拉加什的強勢說起。埃安那圖姆在位時，拉加什打敗了烏瑪，把烏瑪的灌溉渠封堵、把挖渠的人投入水中，烏瑪在南部平原上從此被壓到下風；這份勝勢在《禿鷹碑》上記得清清楚楚，也讓後來的拉加什執政者自居於眾城之上的位置。恩安那圖姆接位後要鞏固權柄，修復並擴建寧基爾蘇的神廟——廟產、祭司與土地是拉加什經濟的骨架，而拉加什城邦的合法性正建立在其對水的調配上。烏瑪這邊，執政者烏爾盧瑪把城與鄉的生存押在一條渠上：引水權就是收成，收成就是政權。當烏瑪一方的開渠越過兩城之間的傳統界線，拉加什用堵渠回應，等於直接宣告烏瑪的主權無效；於是原本可以靠引水慢慢談的邊界問題，被拉加什一方升格成必須由戰爭與神判解決的國恥。這就是第一次烏瑪獨立戰爭的爆發點：推力不是領土野心，而是水界、廟產與城邦尊嚴三件事纏在一起，最後要靠兵戎與神諭了斷。
causeEn: The outbreak has to be explained from the strength of Lagash. In the time of Eannatum, Lagash defeated Umma, dammed Umma's irrigation canal and threw the men who dug it into the water, and from then on Umma was pushed down in the southern plain; that success is set out plainly on the Stele of Vultures, and it allowed the later rulers of Lagash to place themselves above the other cities. Enannatum on his accession needed to consolidate his position, to restore and enlarge the temple of Ningirsu - temple estates, priests and land were the skeleton of the Lagash economy, and the legitimacy of the city rested precisely on its control of the water. On the Umma side the ensi Ur-Lumma staked the survival of the city and its countryside on a single channel: the right to the water was the harvest, and the harvest was the government. When the digging on the Umma side crossed the traditional line between the two cities, Lagash answered with a dam, which amounted to a direct declaration that Umma's sovereignty was void. A boundary question that might have been settled slowly by negotiation over the water was thus raised by the Lagash side into a matter of national humiliation that could only be settled by war and by judgement of the god. That is the flashpoint of the first war of independence of Umma: the push was not territorial ambition, but the entanglement of the water boundary, the temple estate and the standing of the city, to be settled at last by arms and by divine pronouncement.
impact: 影響有遠近兩層。近期看，這場戰爭讓拉加什在南部美索不達米亞確立了無人可爭的地位：烏瑪的執政者被撤換，烏瑪的第一次獨立以失敗告終，隨後由祭司出身的伊爾再起兵勢，觸發第二次獨立戰爭，最後在恩安那圖姆之子恩特梅納手下被平定；拉加什的霸權一直維持到二十四世紀末阿卡德崛起、薩爾貢推翻盧伽爾才告終。遠期看，這套打完還要立約的辦法留給了後世：和約不靠實力維持，而靠神的見證與條文（白銀、黃金、界碑、渠道），於是城邦之間的衝突第一次有了可以援引的成文框架；美沙泥板因此成為已知最早的和平條約文本之一，後人研究古代國際關係時反覆回頭引用它。另一條延續很久的線是水利：灌溉渠既是蘇美爾經濟的命脈，也一直是城邦之間爭端的高發地，邊界要靠水來劃定，戰爭也常常為水而起，烏瑪與拉加什的糾葛從此成為蘇美爾政治的主題之一，一直延伸到阿卡德王朝的邊界碑傳統。
impactEn: The effects work on two scales. In the near term, the war left Lagash with an unchallenged position in southern Mesopotamia: the ruler of Umma was removed, Umma's first attempt at independence failed, and Il, who was of priestly origin, promptly rose again and so triggered the second war of independence, which was finally crushed under Entemena, the son of Enannatum. The ascendancy of Lagash lasted until the end of the twenty-fourth century BC, when Akkad rose and Sargon brought down Lagash itself. In the longer term, the practice of making a treaty after the fighting was done left a lasting inheritance: the peace was not to be kept by force but by the witness of the god and by the terms themselves, in silver, in gold, in boundary stelae and in the course of the canals, and for the first time a conflict between city-states acquired a written framework that could be cited. The Mesha tablet thus stands among the oldest known texts of a peace treaty, and it is turned back to again and again by anyone studying ancient international relations. A second thread runs for a long time after: water. Irrigation canals were the life of the Sumerian economy and at the same time the most frequent occasion of dispute between cities, since boundaries were drawn by water and wars were often fought for it; the entanglement of Umma and Lagash became one of the standing themes of Sumerian politics and continued into the boundary-stela tradition of the Akkadian period.
result: 結果是拉加什的軍事勝利與兩城的和約並存。恩安那圖姆麾下在數場交鋒之後擊敗烏爾盧瑪，烏瑪的軍隊退回城垣，戰局再也沒有翻轉；接著由守護神寧基爾蘇的裁決為和約背書：白銀與黃金各一邁納作為賠償，兩城按新規劃重開並延伸穆杜格渠，邊界以界碑標定，和約文本用阿卡德語寫成泥板，於美沙出土。烏爾盧瑪隨即被逐，烏瑪改由伊爾接掌；伊爾不甘示弱，再度進攻拉加什，開啟第二次獨立戰爭，仍以烏瑪的失敗告終，拉加什的宗主地位在恩特梅納治下維持到前24世紀末。就裝備史而言，這十來年沒有新的兵器湧現，銅矛頭長矛、銅斧、鎚形斧、盾牌、銅盔與驢拉戰車仍是全部家當；真正勝出的，是把武器上的優勢轉化為條約與水利秩序的能力。對卡面那件埃及長矛而言，這場戰爭也提示了它的技術座標：早在蘇美爾城邦以銅矛列陣的年代，舊大陸的長矛已經定型，往後數千年只換材質與形制，不換它在戰役中的角色。
resultEn: The result was a military victory for Lagash and a treaty between the two cities, side by side. Under Enannatum, and after several engagements, Ur-Lumma was defeated, the forces of Umma withdrew behind its walls, and the course of the war was never reversed. The peace was then backed by the judgement of the patron god Ningirsu: one mina of silver and one mina of gold as compensation, the Mu-dug canal reopened and extended according to a new plan, the boundary marked out with stelae, and the terms of the treaty written in Akkadian on a clay tablet that was recovered at Mesha. Ur-Lumma was thereupon driven out and Umma was taken over by Il; unwilling to accept this, Il attacked Lagash again and opened the second war of independence, which likewise ended in the defeat of Umma, while the overlordship of Lagash was maintained under Entemena down to the end of the twenty-fourth century BC. As for the history of equipment, no new weapon came forward in those years: the copper-tipped spear, the copper axe, the axe-head, the shield, the copper helmet and the donkey-drawn chariot remained the whole inventory, and what really won was the ability to convert an advantage in arms into a treaty and a settled order of water. For the Egyptian spear on the card, this war also marks out its technical coordinates: by the age when the Sumerian cities were drawing up their ranks with copper-tipped spears, the spear of the Old World had already been fixed in form, and for the thousands of years that followed it was the material and the shape that changed, not the part it played on the field of battle.
